1.pericope_label: I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing

debates.q: What are the mercy and judgment sung of?

sides.view: God’s own, which he never loses in each other; mercy is named first because it goes before
Not praise of God at all but a vow of what kind of king he will be
The requisite attributes of a good monarch, seen first in the divine King
Both are to be blessed alike — as much love in the blows as in the kisses

debates.q: What is the clause asking when God will come?

sides.view: An echo of David’s words when he dared not bring the ark to his house
Far-fetched, and the clause so awkward that some call it spurious; read it of the perfect way coming to him
A confession of dependence — he cannot walk the way unless God comes by grace
God is said to come to men when he fulfils a promise

outliers.view: Turns the vow about the household into a test, observing how many men are as meek as lambs abroad and wasps or tigers at home
Names Augustine’s reading of the opening verse and rejects it, in a chapter where Augustine’s own comment stands beside his

3.pericope_label: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside

debates.q: How specific are these resolutions meant to be?

sides.view: A programme of government — no unjust wars, no sinful alliances, no oppressive taxation
The vow of a despotic monarch, who need only look with desire to have his way
A rule for the eyes of body and mind, fulfilled only in Christ
A man with a triple tongue, who kills the slandered, the hearer and himself
The informer, a familiar figure of the eastern court, matched by the haughty favourite
One to be excluded from all conversation — a rule David himself broke

outliers.view: Passes on the Chaldee image of the slanderer’s triple tongue and its three deadly wounds, with a patristic parallel
Points out that David failed his own resolution, having listened to the slanders brought against Mephibosheth

6.pericope_label: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me

debates.q: What does the word rendered early mean?

sides.view: In the morning — the eastern hour for holding courts of law
Every morning, constantly and continually, in a general reformation
Speedily, as soon as he is on the throne

debates.q: Who is admitted to the house?

sides.view: The truly religious, as privy counsellors and chief officers of state
Those fit to stand as courtiers in the royal presence
The faithful ministers and members on whom Christ’s eyes rest

outliers.view: Contrasts two Roman emperors on the treatment of flatterers, one who encouraged them and one who burned, banished and enslaved them
